mathematics.assertion_tested: For each tested curve E/F_p (one per class-number-one order O, j = j(O) mod p, plus 4 generic controls) and a point G' of prime order q: for every d <= dmax, the set of m in [1, q-1] whose minimal-degree rational map R with x(mP) = R(x(P)) for all P in <G'> has degree exactly d equals S_d = {alpha mod q : alpha in O, N(alpha) = d}, computed independently from (p, t, q, D_O). Secondary finite checks: CM field of t^2-4p equals that of the table order; batched screen agrees with an independent per-m rank test on audited subsets; every found map has deg num = d, deg den = d-1 and denominator s*h^2 with s | x^3+ax+b; m = 2 reproduces the closed-form doubling formula; the order inferred blindly from (trace, degree) of the found multipliers equals the table order.
mathematics.coefficient_domain: F_p exact (numpy int64 with p < 2^14, all products < 2^41; Python ints for polynomials and number theory)
mathematics.conventions: Short Weierstrass y^2 = x^3 + a x + b; O = Z[w], w = (D + sqrt(D))/2, N(x + y w) = x^2 + D x y + (D^2 - D)/4 y^2; relation Y*psi(X) + phi(X) = 0 with deg phi, deg psi <= d; minimal degree = least d with a verified relation; S_d computed via the eigenvalue mu of w on <G'> from pi = (t - vD)/2 + v w acting as 1.
inputs: 13 class-number-one discriminants D in {-3,-4,-7,-8,-11,-12,-16,-19,-27,-28,-43,-67,-163} with j-invariants from src/cm.py
curve/point selection seeds MASTER_SEED=20261026 plus offsets as coded

bounds.verification: every candidate relation checked on all q-1 points

non_claims: Does not prove conjecture C2 (no multipliers beyond endomorphisms) for other primes, degrees, or curves
Does not prove End(E) = O; it tests finite consequences that discriminate O from O_K and Z[pi]
Says nothing about cryptographic-size curves or about discrete logarithms
Correctness of the class-number-one j-table and of Deuring's reduction theorem is supported here only by search-snippet-level literature checks plus the finite consistency checks above

randomness.generator: Python random.Random (curve, prime and point selection; seeds MASTER_SEED + offsets) and numpy.random.default_rng(20261026) (verification sampling and audit subsets)
